chunks: Certain persons from our companions narrated from ʿAbd al-ʿAzim ibn ʿAbdillah al-Hasani, from Malik ibn ʿAmir, from al-Mufaddal ibn Za'idah, from al-Mufaddal ibn ʿUmar, who said:

Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام said: Whoever practices the religion of Allah without hearing from a truthful one, Allah will inevitably consign him to hardship. And whoever claims hearing from other than the door that Allah has opened, then he is a mushrik. And that door is the trusted one over the hidden secret of Allah.

key_terms.الْبَابِ: the divinely designated gate of access to true guidance
key_terms.الْعَنَاءِ: hardship and exhausting difficulty resulting from misguidance
key_terms.الْمَكْنُونِ: concealed and protected from unauthorized access
key_terms.سَمَاعٍ: receiving religious teaching by hearing from an authorized source
key_terms.سِرِّ اللَّهِ: Allah's hidden and guarded divine matter
key_terms.صَادِقٍ: the truthful authority from whom true religion is taken
key_terms.مُشْرِكٌ: one who associates partners with Allah by taking religion from illegitimate authority

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say religion must be taken only from the divinely opened door?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that true religion must be taken through the divinely appointed and truthful authority, not through unauthorized sources. It condemns religious claims made outside the God-opened gate and identifies that gate as the trusted custodian of Allah’s hidden secret, underscoring the doctrine of Imam-based religious authority.
